title: Stability Ceiling on Tailwise Pharmacy Customer Renewal Orders
content:
*Pharmacist clinical-continuity standard.*

For a Tailwise Pharmacy renewal order on a prescription whose class requires a DEA-registered prescriber, the days' supply per fill the renewal asks for is no more than the stability ceiling. The stability ceiling looks at the renewed prescription's open claims and delivered fills.

- **Open claim**: a dispensed fill of the renewed prescription that carries a dispensing-error claim without a refund entry or a free-remake entry against that fill on the pharmacy ledger.
- **Fills delivered**: the renewed prescription's dispensed fills less its fill credit-back entries.

## Ceiling

| Open claims | Fills delivered | Stability ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| none | 5 or more | the class's maximum days' supply per fill |
| none | at least 3 but fewer than 5 | the renewed prescription's days' supply per fill plus 7 days, never more than the class maximum |
| none | fewer than 3 | the renewed prescription's days' supply per fill |
| one or more | any | the renewed prescription's days' supply per fill |

## Worked cases (hypothetical; renewed prescription written for 21 days, class maximum 30 days)

- 6 dispensed fills, 1 fill credit-back entry, no open claim: fills delivered 5, ceiling 30 days.
- 5 dispensed fills, 1 fill credit-back entry, no open claim: fills delivered 4, ceiling 21 plus 7, 28 days.
- 5 dispensed fills, none credited back, one fill showing a wrong-strength claim with no refund or free-remake entry against it: ceiling 21 days.
- Renewed prescription written for 28 days, 4 fills delivered, no open claim: 28 plus 7 is 35, held to the class maximum: 30 days.
